record.original_question: If SK_1(A tensor_F L) vanishes for every field extension L/F, must the index of the central simple algebra A be square-free?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11.4 (Suslin [Sus91, p. 75]). If SK1(A tensor L) = 0 for every extension L/F, then the index of A is square-free.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $A$ be a central simple $F$-algebra. Recall that $A \cong M_n(D)$ for a unique (up to isomorphism) central division $F$-algebra $D$, and the index of $A$ is $\mathrm{ind}(A) = \deg(D) = \sqrt{\dim_F D}$. For any field extension $L/F$, set $A_L = A \otimes_F L$, and let $\mathrm{SK}_1(A_L) = \mathrm{SL}_1(A_L)/[A_L^\times, A_L^\times]$ denote the reduced Whitehead group, where $\mathrm{SL}_1(A_L)$ is the group of elements of $A_L^\times$ of reduced norm $1$.

Prove or disprove: if $\mathrm{SK}_1(A \otimes_F L) = 0$ for every field extension $L/F$, then $\mathrm{ind}(A)$ is square-free (i.e., not divisible by $p^2$ for any prime $p$).
artifact.category_tag: Reduced Whitehead group SK_1 of central simple algebras
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (due to Suslin) remains open in general. It is equivalent to showing that whenever $\mathrm{ind}(A)$ is not square-free, $\mathrm{SK}_1(A_L) \ne 0$ for some extension $L/F$. Merkurjev established the case where the index is divisible by $4$, and further partial results exist for certain primes, but a complete resolution is not known.

status_evidence.title: Suslin's Conjecture on the Reduced Whitehead Group of a Simple Algebra (Merkurjev)
status_evidence.snippet: If ind(A) is not squarefree, Suslin conjectured that SK_1(A) is nontrivial generically. Merkurjev proves the case where 4 divides ind(A).
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: Merkurjev resolved the case 4 | ind(A); general case open.

status_evidence.title: The Group SK1 for Simple Algebras (Merkurjev)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of Suslin's conjecture and progress toward it for central simple algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture remains a guiding open problem in the area, with partial cases settled.
